title: Introduce prefetch gateway and KV rebind surgery to reduce tail latency
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Reduce 99th-tail latency spikes caused by aggressive prefetching and global KV shard rebalance pauses. This ticket introduces a lightweight prefetch gateway that mediates prefetch requests, implements adaptive watermarking to spread load, and a 'KV rebind surgery' flow that performs soft-shard rebindings without global stop-the-world pauses. The goal is to lower tail latency by ~30-50ms under mixed workloads and reduce KV churn on heavy multi-tenant hosts.
motivation: Recent incidents show periodic latency spikes coincident with prefetch storms during model swap and eviction cycles. Current 'all-at-once' rebinds cause KV hotspot thrashing and scheduler stalls. This refactor reduces operational complexity and allows incremental rollout to Dedicated and Private environments.
milestones: Design prefetch gateway API and admission heuristics (feature-flagged)
Implement adaptive watermarking algorithm and unit tests
Add KV rebind soft-path: incremental per-shard handoff and lease shadowing
Integrate gateway with scheduler to throttle prefetch bursts
End-to-end integration tests and loadbench (simulated mixed-tenancy)
Rollout to canary pool + monitor telemetry, iterate on thresholds
acceptance_criteria: Canary shows >=20% reduction in 99th token generation latency compared to baseline under synthetic multimodel load
KV miss-rate during model swap decreases by >=15% on canary hosts
No increased error rate or request timeouts after gateway enabled
Feature gated behind runtime flag; ability to toggle without restart
Comprehensive dashboards (prefetch_rate, kv_rebind_ops, scheduler_throttle) added to Console
risks: Incorrect watermarking thresholds could increase overall latency if overly conservative
Edge-case race in soft rebind can temporarily duplicate leases if handoff isn't atomic
Increased complexity in admission path may add CPU overhead on control-plane threads
Behavioral differences between Hosted and Private deployments (network variability) require tuning
testing_plan: Unit tests for gateway admission heuristics and watermark math
Property tests for shard handoff invariants (no two owners for >50ms)
Loadbench scenarios: bursty prefetch, steady stream, and model-swap churn
Chaos test: interleave rebinds with simulated eviction and node restarts
Canary + staged rollout with metric gates (latency, errors, kv-miss)
rollout_plan: Feature flag off in prod by default
Enable on small canary fleet (5 hosts) for 24 hours
If gates pass, expand to 20% capacity for 48 hours
Full rollout to runtime-1.22 after two successful staging waves
Provide hotfix path to disable gateway remotely via control plane
implementation_notes: Add lightweight in-memory token-bucket per-prefetch-source to smooth bursts
Use epoched lease shadowing for KV rebind: new owner mirrors reads for grace period
Scheduler integration point: prefetch gateway exposes backpressure signal (0..1) that adjusts admission probability
Keep hot path zero-allocation; avoid locks in fast path by using sequence counters
Plan to upstream adaptive watermarking algorithm into existing batch controller for reuse
observability: New metrics: prefetch_admit_rate, prefetch_backpressure, kv_rebind_latency_ms, kv_rebind_conflicts
Dashboards: Prefetch Gateway Overview, KV Rebind Health, Scheduler Backpressure Heatmap
